content.introduction: StockAnalysis.com offers free online stock information for investors, featuring over 130,000 stocks and funds spanning all global markets and exchanges. The platform aims to provide more accurate data, faster site speed, and a better user experience than other investing websites. It includes a 60-day money back guarantee and offers a free tier with access to the stock screener, basic financial statements, market movers, the IPO calendar, and news. The platform does not provide investment advice or promote individual stocks, encouraging users to verify information using company filings. On October 3, 2026, notable stocks include Direct Digital Holdings (DRCT) at $0.91 with a -39.74% change, and Alpha Modus Holdings (AMOD) at $3.49 with a 198.29% change.

StockAnalysis.com is a financial data and research platform covering over 130,000 stocks and funds globally, including every company in the S&P 500. Founded in 2019 by Kris Gunnars—a pen name for Kristjan Mar Gunnarsson, who also manages his own investment firm, Skuggi Capital ehf.—the platform was built on a straightforward premise: retail investors deserve fast, accurate, institutional-quality data without the clutter, aggressive upsells, and bloated interfaces that plague most financial [...] The platform’s stated aim is to become the internet’s best source of free stock data and information for regular investors, with an emphasis on accuracy, ease of use, speed, and integrity. Importantly, StockAnalysis.com explicitly states that it does not provide investment advice and does not promote individual stocks—it presents data points following objective rules and encourages users to verify information using company filings, including filings with the U.S. Securities and Exchange [...] Yes. Unlike many competitors that offer crippled free trials, StockAnalysis.com’s free tier gives you access to the stock screener, basic financial statements (approximately 5 years of S&P-sourced history), market movers, the IPO calendar, and news—all without even creating an account. It’s ad-supported and has limited financial history, but it’s a genuinely functional research tool. Free is strong enough to validate whether you like the workflow and UI before committing to a paid plan.
